title: Anya and Ghosts
statementMd:
Anya loves to watch horror movies. In the best traditions of horror, she will be visited by $*m*$ ghosts tonight. Anya has lots of candles prepared for the visits, each candle can produce light for exactly $*t*$ seconds. It takes the girl one second to light one candle. More formally, Anya can spend one second to light one candle, then this candle burns for exactly $*t*$ seconds and then goes out and can no longer be used.

For each of the $*m*$ ghosts Anya knows the time at which it comes: the $*i*$-th visit will happen $*w*_{*i*}$ seconds after midnight, all $*w*_{*i*}$'s are distinct. Each visit lasts exactly one second.

What is the minimum number of candles Anya should use so that during each visit, at least $*r*$ candles are burning? Anya can start to light a candle at any time that is integer number of seconds from midnight, possibly, at the time before midnight. **That means, she can start to light a candle integer number of seconds before midnight or integer number of seconds after a midnight, or in other words in any integer moment of time.**

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*m*$, $*t*$, $*r*$ ($1 ≤ *m*, *t*, *r* ≤ 300$), representing the number of ghosts to visit Anya, the duration of a candle's burning and the minimum number of candles that should burn during each visit.

The next line contains $*m*$ space-separated numbers $*w*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ *m*$, $1 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 300$), the $*i*$-th of them repesents at what second after the midnight the $*i*$-th ghost will come. All $*w*_{*i*}$'s are distinct, they follow in the strictly increasing order.

## Output

If it is possible to make at least $*r*$ candles burn during each visit, then print the minimum number of candles that Anya needs to light for that.

If that is impossible, print $- 1$.

## Note

**Anya can start lighting a candle in the same second with ghost visit. But this candle isn't counted as burning at this visit.**

It takes exactly one second to light up a candle and only after that second this candle is considered burning; it means that if Anya starts lighting candle at moment x, candle is buring from second x + 1 to second x + t inclusively.

In the first sample test three candles are enough. For example, Anya can start lighting them at the $3$-rd, $5$-th and $7$-th seconds after the midnight.

In the second sample test one candle is enough. For example, Anya can start lighting it one second before the midnight.

In the third sample test the answer is $- 1$, since during each second at most one candle can burn but Anya needs three candles to light up the room at the moment when the ghost comes.
statementZhMd:
Anya 喜欢观看恐怖电影。按照恐怖故事的最佳传统，今晚将有 $*m*$ 个幽灵来拜访她。Anya 准备了许多蜡烛，每根蜡烛恰好可以照明 $*t*$ 秒。点燃一根蜡烛需要花费女孩一秒钟。更正式地说，Anya 可以用一秒钟点燃一根蜡烛，随后这根蜡烛燃烧恰好 $*t*$ 秒，然后熄灭且不能再次使用。

Anya 知道每个幽灵到来的时间：第 $*i*$ 次拜访将在午夜后的 $*w*_{*i*}$ 秒发生，所有 $*w*$'s 互不相同。每次拜访恰好持续一秒。

为了使每次拜访期间至少有 $*r*$ 根蜡烛在燃烧，Anya 至少需要使用多少根蜡烛？Anya 可以在从午夜开始计数的任意整数秒时刻点燃蜡烛，也可以在午夜之前开始点燃。**这意味着，她可以在午夜前若干个整数秒或午夜后的若干个整数秒开始点燃蜡烛，换句话说，她可以在任意整数时刻开始点燃蜡烛。**

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*m*$、$*t*$、$*r*$（$1 ≤ *m* , *t* , *r* ≤ 300$），分别表示 Anya 要接待的幽灵数量、每根蜡烛的燃烧时长，以及每次拜访期间至少需要燃烧的蜡烛数量。

下一行包含 $*m*$ 个用空格分隔的整数 $*w*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *m*$，$1 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 300$），其中第 $*i*$ 个数表示第 $*i*$ 个幽灵将在午夜后的第几秒到来。所有 $*w*$'s 互不相同，并且严格递增。

## 输出格式

如果可以使每次拜访期间至少有 $*r*$ 根蜡烛燃烧，则输出 Anya 为此需要点燃的蜡烛的最少数量。

如果无法做到，则输出 $- 1$。

## 说明

**Anya 可以在幽灵拜访的同一秒开始点燃蜡烛。但这根蜡烛在本次拜访时不计入燃烧中的蜡烛。**

点燃一根蜡烛恰好需要一秒，只有在这一秒之后，这根蜡烛才会被视为正在燃烧；也就是说，如果 Anya 在时刻 x 开始点燃蜡烛，那么它将在第 x + 1 秒至第 x + t 秒（含两端）燃烧。

在第一个样例中，三根蜡烛就足够了。例如，Anya 可以在午夜后的第 3、5、7 秒开始点燃它们。

在第二个样例中，一根蜡烛就足够了。例如，Anya 可以在午夜前一秒开始点燃它。

在第三个样例中，答案是 $- 1$，因为每秒至多只能有一根蜡烛燃烧，而在幽灵到来时，Anya 需要点燃三根蜡烛来照亮房间。
